newsitem.title: GERMANY: Little trade in German wheat but prices steadier.
newsitem.headline: Little trade in German wheat but prices steadier.

text.p: German wheat brokers reported little new trade in early 1997 but prices were steadier in line with some anticipated west and east European demand.
Transport of wheat was disrupted on iced-up inland canals and at export terminals, creating premiums for spot delivery, brokers said.
The Hamburg grain exchange after a two-week break marked up its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) by 2.50 marks per tonne to 280 and spot feed wheat by 2.50 to 275, free Hamburg.
European prices were further underpinned by a firm sterling which made British feed wheat slightly less competitive and by firm U.S. levels on fears of winter kill in some regions.
But brokers saw only limited upside potential in early 1997 prices because of German premiums over other west European origins and seller reluctance to pay for storage costs.
They were also looking for direction from Thursday's weekly EU export meeting. The EU at the last tender on Dec 19 dropped the wheat rebate to 11.94 Ecus/tonne from 17.47 previously.

In the fob Baltic export market, brokers put normal spot bread wheat (12 percent protein) for first half January at 285-287.50 marks and higher quality offers at around 292-308, depending on protein levels.
Barley markets took some support from a new Saudi purchasing tender for 1.2 million tonnes of Jan/Feb material.
Fob Baltic barley was quoted slightly higher at 255-271 marks.
Fob rye offers were quietly unchanged at 252.50-265 marks. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
